highlightAliases.old: 3 tiers by comorbidity/function/cognition: Good, Intermediate, Poor health.
highlightAliases.new: 3 tiers by comorbidity/function/cognition: Good, Intermediate, Poor health; Current practice (not the book): individualize targets (grade C): healthy older adults with few stable illnesses and intact cognition/function should have lower goals such as A1C <7.0-7.5% and/or CGM time in 70-180 mg/dL ≥70% and time ≤70 mg/dL ≤4%; complex/intermediate health prioritizes hypoglycemia avoidance, with less stringent goals such as A1C <8.0%, time in 70-180 mg/dL ≥50% and time <70 mg/dL <1%, considering cognition/function, frailty, comorbidity, medication risk-benefit and preferences; very complex/poor health avoids reliance on A1C and focuses on avoiding hypoglycemia and symptomatic hyperglycemia, with no numerical CGM goal specified; fasting/premeal and bedtime ranges respectively are 80-130/80-180 mg/dL (healthy), 90-150/100-180 (complex/intermediate) and 100-180/110-200 (very complex/poor); lower A1C goals require no recurrent/severe hypoglycemia or undue treatment burden - ADA Standards of Care 2026, Section 13, recommendations 13.7a-c pS282 and Table 13.2 pS284

highlightAliases.old: Sulfonylureas (e.g., glipizide 2.5–10 mg qd–BID) (p1577). Cautions: hypoglycemia; avoid glyburide — long half-life, not recommended in older adults (p1579); avoid in renal/hepatic impairment (p1579).
highlightAliases.new: Sulfonylureas (e.g., glipizide 2.5–10 mg qd–BID) (p1577). Cautions: hypoglycemia; avoid glyburide — long half-life, not recommended in older adults (p1579); avoid in renal/hepatic impairment (p1579); Required reading: see AGS Beers 2023 required-article card for qualified sulfonylurea avoidance and the preference if one is used (Table 2, p2061)

highlightAliases.old: Metformin / metformin ER: printed dose lines 500–1000 mg BID, max 2500 mg/d, 500–2000 mg qd — the page does not pair each line to an agent (p1577). Cautions: avoid if eGFR <30; avoid in unstable heart failure/acute illness (lactic-acidosis risk) (p1576).
highlightAliases.new: Metformin / metformin ER: printed dose lines 500–1000 mg BID, max 2500 mg/d, 500–2000 mg qd — the page does not pair each line to an agent (p1577). Cautions: avoid if eGFR <30; avoid in unstable heart failure or during acute hospitalization for major illness that could reduce tissue perfusion (lactic-acidosis risk) (p1576).

highlightAliases.old: CVD-outcome-proven drug classes (large CVOTs, average participant age >60): SGLT-2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, canagliflozin, dapagliflozin) and GLP-1 agonists (liraglutide, semaglutide, dulaglutide) (p1571).
highlightAliases.new: CVD-outcome-proven drug classes (large CVOTs, average participant age >60): SGLT-2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, canagliflozin, dapagliflozin) and GLP-1 agonists (liraglutide, semaglutide, dulaglutide) (p1570–1571).

highlightAliases.old: Cognitive screening at diagnosis, then annually if borderline or every 2–3 years if normal (p1568).
highlightAliases.new: The chapter gives annual follow-up after a borderline cognitive screen and every 2–3 years after a normal screen (p1568). ADA 2026 recommends an initial screen and annual screening from age 65, with additional assessment when self-management changes.

highlightAliases.old: BP target <140/90 mmHg for most; consider 130/80 mmHg for high-risk (prior stroke, progressing CKD), with orthostatic monitoring (p1572).
highlightAliases.new: Hazzard gives a BP goal below 140/90 mmHg for most (p1572). ADA 2026 recommends below 130/80 mmHg when safely attainable. For poor health, limited life expectancy or high treatment risk, a goal such as below 140/90 may be appropriate. Check standing BP (ADA 2026, recommendation 13.9).
